opportunities.query_text: The Financial Times has commissioned me to write an analysis article on how, as management consulting firms lean more on AI, their business clients are demanding/will demand a reduction in consulting fees. I think it's a really interesting subject. I'm pretty sure people have some strong views on it! NB: My article is focused on UK management consulting firms. Who I'm looking to talk to: - A couple of UK businesses who say they've demanded/will demand that their UK management consultant firm cuts fees/changes its fees to reflect AI use - 2-3 management consulting firms who do business in the UK (How AI is changing/will change their fees; or maybe it won't? As AI automates an growing proportion of consulting tasks - data analysis, idea generation, strategy advice... how are firms justifying to clients their fees and any fee increases?) - An AI/tech expert with deep knowledge of how consulting firms are using AI in their business, estimates for how much time/productivity benefits AI creates, whether consultants are adjusting their fees in response to greater AI use.
opportunities.deadline: Not explicitly stated (appears active/recent based on Sourcee listing)
opportunities.contact_method: Email (redacted on Sourcee) or DM via original platform
opportunities.relevance_notes: Directly about AI cost impact on business pricing — the core thesis that AI tool adoption should reduce fees, not increase them. AIToolsEssentials' verified pricing data shows AI tools are getting cheaper (API costs down ~10x, Gemini Ultra dropped from $250 to $100) while subscriptions multiply. Can offer the perspective that as AI tools commoditize, the businesses passing on AI cost savings to clients will win. The overlap/stack audit angle applies: consulting firms using 5+ AI tools are paying for overlap, and clients should demand that inefficiency doesn't get passed to them.
opportunities.suggested_pitch_template: Template 1 (AI Tool Pricing Changes, reactive) — adapted: pitch as an 'AI/tech expert with deep knowledge of how AI tools are used in business.' Offer verified data on AI tool pricing trends (API costs down 10x, Gemini Ultra $250→$100, ChatGPT Go at $8/mo, GitHub Copilot moving to usage-based credits). Frame the argument: AI tools are commoditizing, so consulting firms that lean on AI should be passing savings to clients, not maintaining fees. Offer the Stack Audit framework as evidence that most businesses overpay for AI tool overlap — consulting firms are no exception. Note: journalist wants UK-focused sources, so acknowledge UK market context if pitching.

opportunities.query_text: Where Business Leaders Focus Their Tech Budgets As Tech Stock Market Volatility Persists. Tech stocks continue on a volatile trajectory, with Goldman Sachs reporting that hedge funds are selling US tech stocks at a record pace, and Bloomberg reporting that big tech needs to justify AI spending. Meanwhile, small, medium, and large business leaders, decision-makers, and executives, who are modernizing their tech and operations, are left to figure out the road ahead. Amid this volatility, a new report from Forrester Research agrees that tech leaders face 'sustained pressure to deliver value, modernize for AI, govern at speed, and maintain trust — all amid persistent volatility and budget scrutiny'. However, the same report found that more than 80% of business and technology leaders expect budget increases for 2027, highlighting strategic areas of investment for next year. For this report, I am looking for expert sources to provide clear signals for small, medium, and large business owners and decision-makers to help them navigate the current landscape and plan for 2027.
opportunities.relevance_notes: Directly about AI spending and budget decisions for businesses. AIToolsEssentials' core value proposition is helping businesses decide which AI tools to keep, cut, and replace — exactly the 'clear signals' this journalist is seeking. The Stack Audit provides a concrete framework for budget scrutiny. Verified pricing data on 74+ tools with keep/cut verdicts is a directly citeable resource. The Forrester data about 80% expecting budget increases for 2027 aligns with the overlap problem: more budget without an audit means more overlap spend.
opportunities.suggested_pitch_template: Template 2 (Overlapping Subscriptions / Cost Optimization) — adapted: pitch as an expert source on 'where business leaders should focus AI tech budgets for 2027.' Offer the keep/cut framework: most teams don't need more AI budget, they need to audit what they already pay for. Cite common overlaps (Copilot Pro $10 + Cursor Pro $20 + Claude Max $100 = $130/mo for same coding job). Offer Stack Audit data showing the average team carries 2-3 overlapping subscriptions. Frame: 'The clear signal for 2027 budget planning is not which new AI tools to buy, but which existing subscriptions to cut before adding more.'

opportunities.query_text: The biggest AI problem isn't the AI. Went for 'Demo to Dollars'... Expected to learn about: usage-based pricing, subscriptions, AI monetisation. Instead, the biggest takeaway was something much simpler. Data architecture... As subscription models that worked for SaaS are starting to fracture forecasting becomes ever more so relevant... Right now I'm on a mission to collect 10 real SME operational problems that AI could solve. If you run an SME and there's a repetitive task or messy process in your business: Drop it in the comments or DM me.
opportunities.journalist_publication: Independent (posted via LinkedIn, appears to be a content creator/researcher)
opportunities.relevance_notes: About SaaS subscription models fracturing and AI solving SME operational problems. The 'subscription models that worked for SaaS are starting to fracture' observation directly connects to AIToolsEssentials' coverage of AI pricing shifts (usage-based credits, tier splits, per-outcome pricing). Can offer data on how AI tool pricing is moving away from flat subscriptions toward usage-based and tiered models. The SME operational problems angle is a fit for the Stack Audit.
opportunities.suggested_pitch_template: Template 1 (AI Tool Pricing Changes, reactive) — adapted: offer the observation that AI tool subscriptions are indeed fracturing — from flat $20/mo to usage-based credits (GitHub Copilot AI Credits), per-outcome pricing (HubSpot Breeze $0.50/resolved conversation), and multi-tier splits (ChatGPT 7 tiers, Claude 7 tiers). Pitch the Stack Audit as a tool for SMEs to navigate this fracturing by identifying which subscription model actually fits their usage. Offer to contribute one of the 10 SME operational problems: 'SMEs paying for overlapping AI tool subscriptions without realizing it.'

summary: Two new high-relevance opportunities found this run. (1) Financial Times commissioned an article on how management consulting firms leaning on AI face client demands for fee reductions — directly about AI cost impact on business pricing, and AIToolsEssentials' verified AI tool pricing data (API costs down 10x, Gemini Ultra $250→$100, usage-based model shifts) is strong evidence. (2) Forbes seeking expert sources on where business leaders should focus tech budgets for 2027 amid AI spending scrutiny — the Stack Audit keep/cut framework is exactly the 'clear signal' they want. Both are strong fits. One medium opportunity: SME/SaaS subscription fracturing (open deadline, collecting case studies). One low-medium: The Financial Brand on AI + subscription models in banking (tight Sept 22 deadline, but banking focus is a stretch). Two low-relevance AI requests (workplace fraud, AI data surveillance) — skip. Previously reported FinOps/AI cost overruns request still visible and high-relevance — pitch if not yet done. Forbes dynamic pricing request likely expired (Wednesday deadline). HARO remains email-gated, Connectively requires login, Qwoted requires login, Source of Sources is email-only, X Search credits exhausted. Sourcee.app remains the best accessible aggregation source. Recommend: (1) pitch FT consulting fees + AI costs request ASAP — strongest new fit, (2) pitch Forbes business tech budgets / AI spending request — second strongest, (3) pitch SME SaaS subscription fracturing if time permits, (4) if FinOps/AI cost overruns not yet pitched from last run, do it now, (5) George should subscribe to HARO email digest and Source of Sources for direct access to email-gated queries.
